costs.how: 5 bps each time we buy or sell, 4 times

test_year.reason: The original study's test-year results were known by 2026-10-02; the five-check rule was written on 2026-10-04, after that. So the test year helped shape the rule and is not a clean out-of-sample test.

clean_check.reason: The rule and its settings were frozen before this data was used, and were not changed after.

slippage.summary: Daily data cannot measure slippage. Both standard estimators find no spread on most contracts and months (it is smaller than a normal day's price noise), and with negative readings set to zero they give 26–31 bps for every contract alike, which is the day's volatility, not a spread. The hard floor is half a tick: at most 0.34 bps. Our trades were a median 0.06% of the day's volume. Training breaks even at 5.3 bps per order. Only real broker fills (a forward test) can settle the number.

multiple_testing.note: 18 settings × 6 pairs = 108 were tried on training only (that is tuning, not testing). On the test year, 3 rule versions were scored (original study, five checks, five checks + switch). t = 0.40 on 17 trades gives p = 0.694 (two-sided); allowing for 3 looks, p = 1.00. Not significant either way.

switch.note: GOLDM · GOLDPETAL: training made +₹19,793 over 14 trades (t = 0.84; 83% of resamples above zero), close to a coin flip, so the switch is a weak filter, not proof.

petal_break.summary: GOLDGUINEA − GOLDPETAL fell from +203 to +19 bps between 04 Nov 2024 and 11 Nov 2024, inside one contract (expiry Nov 2024). Against GOLDM over the same days, GOLDPETAL rose about 249 bps and GOLDGUINEA about 66 bps, so most of the move was GOLDPETAL repricing. The gap swung back part-way for a few weeks, then settled: median +255 bps from May 2024 to Nov 2024, −29 bps from Feb 2025 to Jul 2025. We found no MCX notice explaining it, so the cause is not confirmed.

stages.name: Load & Validate
stages.desc: Parse 47,521 daily prices: 35,014 from the MCX history book (2011–2023) and 12,507 from our own MCX download (Oct 2023 on). Strip symbols, check primary keys, compare against the raw MCX file and the book, flag no-trade days.

stages.name: Normalize
stages.desc: Divide the Bhavcopy close by the grams it is quoted for and by its purity (from a date-effective specification table) to get a price per gram of pure gold.

stages.name: Implied Carry
stages.desc: Estimate the cost of carry from GOLDPETAL calendar spreads, skipping contracts inside their tender window; forward-fill only. Estimates outside 0–15% a year are flagged as unstable.

stages.name: Pair Construction
stages.desc: Pick contracts using the previous day's open interest, so nothing from the future is used.

stages.name: Point-in-Time z-scores
stages.desc: One rolling mean and spread for alerts, charts and backtest, from earlier days only.

stages.name: One rule: five checks
stages.desc: The same five checks drive today's alerts and every backtest trade: enough history, an unusual gap that is not already past the stop-loss, a gap bigger than 2× the round-trip cost, liquidity sized to the trade (each leg at most 5% of that day's volume), and contract life (each leg clear of its own tender window).

stages.name: Train/test split and historical holdout
stages.desc: Settings chosen once on Train (2023-10 to 2025-09) by highest net after costs, then frozen for the test year (2025-10 to 2026-09) and for the historical holdout (2011–2023). There is no separate validation period and no rolling re-fit, so this is a single split, not a rolling walk-forward. A pair is traded in Test only if training gave at least 10 trades and a profit.

stages.name: Costs & Attribution
stages.desc: Each closed trade is split into spread and gold parts after statutory costs and slippage; every trade is also marked to market daily for portfolio figures. No fills on days a leg moved 6% or more, except a flagged forced exit before a tender window.

rules: Rolling z uses only t-1 and earlier observations (shifted window)
Contract pairing selects max min(OI) as of t-1
Parameters tuned strictly on in-sample Train data and frozen; the on/off switch also uses Train only
Signals generated at close t execute at close t+1; exits never fill at the signal's own close
No fills on days either leg moved 6% or more (prices may be stuck at the daily limit)
Carry rate c_t is forward-filled only; never backward-filled

A position opens only if both legs are at least 9 trading days from expiry on the signal day, and is closed by the last trading day before either leg's 5-day tender window (the calendar is known in advance, so this uses no future data)
limits: Prices are the Bhavcopy close: a daily reference, not an executable fill. We have not verified that it equals MCX's official settlement price in every period.

Bhavcopy volume indicates activity but does not measure order-book depth or guarantee execution; the size check (each leg at most 5% of the day's volume) is a screen, not a fill model. Open interest is only a screen. Slippage is assumed at 5 bps per order: daily data cannot measure it (see the slippage check), only real broker fills can.

Tender periods: no MCX circular could be read directly (MCX refuses automated requests). Broker notices report 5 trading days (2025) and 3 days (from Feb 2026) for the smaller gold contracts; we apply the longer 5-day window to every contract and year. Contract specifications before Oct 2023 are assumed equal to today's (no source found).

The 2025–26 test year is not a clean out-of-sample test: the five-check rule was written on 2026-10-04, after the original study's test-year results were known. The 2011–2023 historical holdout was never used to choose settings, but the Oct-2026 lifecycle and liquidity correction was made after the earlier version's results there were known.
GOLDTEN contracts listed only on 31-Mar-2025, offering limited historical depth.
Test period contains only 2 to 4 trades per pair (17 in total); small samples preclude high certainty.

GOLDPETAL repriced against the other contracts: GOLDGUINEA − GOLDPETAL fell from +203 to +19 bps between 04 Nov 2024 and 11 Nov 2024, inside one contract (expiry Nov 2024). Against GOLDM over the same days, GOLDPETAL rose about 249 bps and GOLDGUINEA about 66 bps, so most of the move was GOLDPETAL repricing. The gap swung back part-way for a few weeks, then settled: median +255 bps from May 2024 to Nov 2024, −29 bps from Feb 2025 to Jul 2025. We found no MCX notice explaining it, so the cause is not confirmed.
Trades closed during the Jan–Mar 2026 crash made −₹33,564 of the test-year result (−₹57,003 in total). The crash window was named after the results were seen, so this split is a check, not a test.

The training switch rests on thin evidence: GOLDM · GOLDPETAL: training made +₹19,793 over 14 trades (t = 0.84; 83% of resamples above zero), close to a coin flip, so the switch is a weak filter, not proof.
When the pair series switches to new contracts, open trades are closed; this adds cost.
Exchange transaction charges and statutory rates should be regularly verified against MCX circulars.
conclusion: Cross-contract gold gaps are real and measurable, but no persistent edge is proven after costs. The historical holdout is 2011–2023: the settings were chosen on training data only and that period was never used to choose them. There the rule lost ₹1,30,655 over 88 trades at 5 bps slippage (t = −2.04). The 2025–26 test year lost ₹57,003 over 17 trades, but it is not a clean test: the five-check rule was written after that year's first results were seen. It is not significant either way (t = 0.40, p = 0.69, or 1.00 allowing for the 3 rule versions scored on that year). In training the same rule made ₹3,775 over 33 trades, and training would have switched on only 1 of 6 pairs. In Oct 2026 the contract-lifecycle and liquidity rules were corrected (tender windows, size-aware volume checks); that was done after the earlier version's results on every period were known, to fix the rules, not to change the results.
